literal: Two different [are] the world's nature: wealth [is] different, clear-minded ones becoming also [is] different.
translation: The nature of the world takes two different forms: the amassing of wealth is one thing, and the attainment of clear wisdom is another.
modern: உலகத்தின் இயற்கை இரண்டு வேறுபட்ட நிலைகளைக் கொண்டது: செல்வம் உடையவராக இருப்பது வேறு, தெளிந்த அறிவுடையவராக இருப்பது வேறு.
explanation: This couplet observes the fundamental disconnect between material wealth and intellectual clarity in the world. The phrase 'இருவேறு இயற்கை' (two different natures) establishes that the world operates on divergent paths. 'திரு' (wealth) and 'தெள்ளியர் ஆதல்' (becoming clear-minded) are explicitly contrasted as 'வேறு... வேறு' (different... different). It implies that the forces of destiny distribute riches and wisdom independently, so that the wealthy are not necessarily wise, and the wise are not necessarily wealthy.
